markets.rules_primary: If an adopted Colorado Attorney General rule implementing the Automated Decision-Making Technology Act (SB 26-189) that at minimum clarifies the Act's post-adverse-outcome disclosure requirements is enacted in Colorado before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Enactment requires completion of all constitutional and legal requirements for the legislation to become binding law.

Standard legislation requiring executive approval: final passage by all required legislative bodies, executive signature OR becoming law despite executive inaction OR successful veto override, and satisfaction of any required waiting periods
Legislation not requiring executive approval: final passage and completion of required waiting periods
Constitutional amendments: passage with required supermajorities and completion of ratification processes
Executive orders: official signature, publication in official government records, and legal effectiveness
Administrative regulations: completion of required rulemaking procedures, final publication in the official government record, and legal effectiveness

The following do NOT constitute enactment:

Legislative passage without completed executive action
Passage by only some required bodies
Provisional passage
Non-binding resolutions
Draft orders

Enactment occurs when all requirements are completed, regardless of pending judicial challenges.

Note: This event was issued before the September 14, 2026 amendment to the LAW Contract, so that amendment does not apply. To be clear, a law must take legal effect before this event’s deadline; a law enacted before the deadline whose effective date falls on or after it does not satisfy the Payout Criterion.

custom_strike.Topic: Renton, Washington ends its use of Flock Safety license plate reader cameras

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Renton, Washington ends its use of Flock Safety license plate reader cameras after Issuance and before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A jurisdiction ends its use of Flock Safety cameras if its governing body, chief executive, or police department:

terminates a Flock Safety contract before the contract's scheduled end date, or
declines to renew or extend a Flock Safety contract, or declines to allow an automatic renewal to take effect, or
allows a Flock Safety contract to reach its scheduled end date without entering a renewal or replacement agreement, or
otherwise discontinues the jurisdiction's use of Flock Safety cameras, including by moving to a different license plate reader vendor.

The action must occur on or after August 21, 2026, and be reported before February 1, 2027.

The following do NOT count:

Renewing or extending the contract, even with added privacy safeguards, audit requirements or use restrictions
A temporary pause, camera deactivation, or moratorium that leaves the underlying contract in force and does not prevent its renewal
A non-binding resolution, advisory referendum or committee recommendation that the official empowered to act has not acted upon

Each jurisdiction is judged on its own, and action by a jurisdiction not named in this event does not affect any market here.

Only reporting from a Source Agency qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.
markets.title: Will it be reported by a Source Agency that Renton, Washington ends its use of Flock Safety license plate reader cameras before Feb 1, 2027?

markets.rules_primary: If Hawaii’s total visitor arrivals for calendar year 2026 are above 9.4 million, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Underlying is total statewide visitor arrivals for calendar year 2026, including visitors arriving by air and visitors arriving aboard out-of-state cruise ships, as reported by the State of Hawaii. It does not use visitor days, average daily census, airport passenger throughput, or arrivals to an individual island. Visitors who fly to Hawaii to board a cruise ship are already included in air arrivals and are not separately added again.

Resolution uses the first publication containing complete January–December 2026 data; subsequent revisions do not affect resolution. DBEDT’s 2025 total, for example, was 9,642,991 = 9,493,213 by air + 149,778 by cruise ship.

markets.rules_primary: If the US personal saving rate is reported below 2.0% in any Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Income and Outlays release covering a 2026 reference month, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The “US personal saving rate” means the monthly personal saving rate reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, defined as personal saving as a percentage of disposable personal income.

This market resolves based on the first value reported for each 2026 reference month in the corresponding BEA Personal Income and Outlays release. Later revisions do not affect settlement.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the economic data is released.
markets.rules_primary: If the M2 money-supply growth for December 2026 is below 5.0%, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
For purposes of this market, “M2 money-supply growth” means the year-over-year percent change in the seasonally adjusted M2 money stock for December 2026, calculated using FRED series M2SL.

The year-over-year percent change will be calculated as follows: December 2026 M2SL divided by December 2025 M2SL, minus one, expressed as a percentage and rounded to one decimal place.

This market will use the first value published by FRED for December 2026. Revisions released after the first publication of the December 2026 value will not be considered.

markets.rules_primary: If Arch Manning is announced to be staying at Texas after Issuance and before Feb 2, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Stays at Texas: Resolves Yes if Arch Manning officially withdraws his name from the NCAA Transfer Portal or announces withdrawal, AND is enrolled and on the roster after Issuance and before Feb 2, 2027. If Arch Manning never enters the transfer portal and remains on his current team by Feb 2, 2027, then the market for staying with his current team will resolve to Yes.
Declare for the Draft: Resolves Yes if Arch Manning declares for the NFL Draft after Issuance and before Feb 2, 2027, as reported by a Source Agency. 
Commits/Transfers to Another School: If Arch Manning officially commits or transfers to another school after Issuance and before Feb 2, 2027, as reported by a Source Agency, then the market for that school resolves to Yes.
Retires / Not enrolled at a DI school: Resolves early if there is a public announcement of retirement or ending their football career, as reported by a Source Agency. Otherwise, if Arch Manning has not qualified for any of the special outcomes outlined above, and is not enrolled at a DI school on Feb 2, 2027, then the "Retires / Not enrolled at a DI school" market resolves to Yes.
A school commitment counts even if Arch Manning later decommits or never enrolls. Rumors and visits do not count. If Arch Manning re-enters the portal, the first announced commitment or enrollment controls.

Kalshi is not affiliated, associated, authorized, endorsed by, or in any way officially connected with the NCAA. All trademarks, logos, and brand names are the property of their respective owners.

markets.rules_primary: If the Republican party has below 45 Senate seats on Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Clarification (11/12/26): Kalshi has filed an amendment to this market's Contract so that it can settle before February 1, 2027 once the election results have decided it. Starting November 26, 2026, Kalshi will check each party's seat count every day at 10:00 AM ET using Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). Any market the results have decided will settle that morning; the rest will settle on February 1, 2027 as they do now. If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If Gina Hinojosa, as Governor of Texas, orders a freeze on residential electricity rates in Texas after Issuance and before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
Ordering a freeze means Gina Hinojosa, acting as Governor of Texas, signs an executive order or proclamation, or issues a formal written directive to the Public Utility Commission of Texas or another state agency, that holds residential electricity rates in Texas at their current levels. A freeze covering only some residential customers or only part of the residential bill counts. The order need not take effect, remain in force, or survive a court challenge. Announcements, pledges, legislative proposals, a disaster or emergency declaration that does not itself freeze residential electricity rates, and orders limited to gas or diesel taxes, data center permits or wholesale prices do NOT count.

Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the Texas Senate adopts a rule or resolution transferring powers from the lieutenant governor before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A rule or resolution adopted by a vote of the Texas Senate counts, whether temporary or permanent, as recorded in the Senate Journal. No statute, House action, or Governor action is required.

It qualifies if it removes any of the following powers from the lieutenant governor, in whole or in part, or makes the power shared with, or subject to approval by, the Senate, any senator, a Senate committee, or a party caucus:

Appointing the members or chairs of standing committees
Appointing the members of Senate conference committees
Referring bills to committees
Deciding the order in which bills are taken up on the Senate floor

The following do NOT qualify:

A rules package that leaves these powers with the lieutenant governor
A change only to the vote required to take up a bill (for example, the five-ninths vote) that does not move the power to decide the order of consideration
A change only to how the Senate operates when the lieutenant governor is absent
A change to powers the Texas Constitution or state statutes give to the office

The adoption date is the date of the Senate vote, not any effective date.
markets.title: Will the Texas Senate strip the lieutenant governor's powers before Feb 1, 2027?

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if all elections have been certified.
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of Hakeem Jeffries in the Speaker election and Chuck Schumer in the Senate Majority Leader election win their respective elections in the 120th Congress Speaker of the House and Senate Majority Leader elections by Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
The Speaker election is the election for Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives at the opening of the 120th Congress. A person receives a vote when the roll call record of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives, or a Source Agency report of that record, shows a vote cast for that person on a roll call to elect the Speaker at the opening of the 120th Congress. Every ballot held until a Speaker is elected counts, and one vote on any of them counts. A Member voting for themself counts, and so does a vote for a person who is not a Member of the House. If a Speaker is elected at the opening of the 120th Congress and the Clerk's record of those ballots shows no vote for this person, the market resolves to No once the Speaker is elected; a later report does not reopen it.

The following do NOT count:
A vote recorded as Present or Not Voting

A vote for a name that does not identify this person alone, such as a surname shared by other Members, unless the record identifies them
A vote in a party caucus or conference election
A roll call to elect a Speaker after the opening of the Congress, such as to fill a vacancy
A pledge, petition, or statement of support without a recorded vote

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the government is officially formed.
markets.rules_primary: If a coalition that includes the People's Party make up the next elected ruling government of Spain before Jan 1, 2028, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A party is considered to be part of government if one or more of its representatives hold at least one ministerial or cabinet-level position (including junior ministers or equivalent executive roles, if applicable) in the new government. This evaluation shall occur at the first official, stable formation of the government (i.e., once the legislative process for forming a government is complete and the head of state appoints ministers under normal non-caretaker circumstances).

Additionally,
A “confidence and supply arrangement” (or any analogous agreement), where a party does not hold formal cabinet or ministerial positions but has publicly agreed, through a formal written agreement or a widely recognized, explicitly stated political deal, to support the government on key votes (e.g., votes of confidence, budget/finance bills) without formally joining the cabinet or government, may be included in the Payout Criterion if specified in parties (e.g. parties could take the form of “The Conservative Party and the Liberal Party” as well as “The Conservative Party with the support of the Greens”).
If, following the election, a caretaker or interim government is appointed temporarily before the formal government formation, this caretaker period does not count for determining a given party's status.

No market on this event specifies a confidence and supply arrangement. For the purposes of this event:

A party whose representatives hold at least one ministerial or cabinet-level position resolves to Yes. In Spain, a minister (ministro or ministra) or a secretary of state (secretario or secretaria de Estado) appointed by Royal Decree holds a qualifying position
A party that only supports the government from outside it, under a confidence and supply or investiture-support agreement, and holds no ministerial or cabinet-level position, does NOT count
Advisers and cabinet staff are NOT ministerial or cabinet-level positions
Holding seats in the Cortes Generales is neither required nor sufficient

The government evaluated is the first government formed following the Spanish general election of November 29, 2026. The outgoing government that remains in office until that government is appointed is a caretaker government and does not count. Frente Amplio is the electoral coalition of Movimiento Sumar, Izquierda Unida, Más Madrid and Comuns; the Frente Amplio market resolves Yes if a qualifying officeholder is a member of any party that submitted the Frente Amplio list, and that officeholder also counts toward their own party's market where one is listed. Otherwise, each officeholder is attributed to the party of which that officeholder is a member, as recorded in official government sources or, if those are silent, in a formal coalition agreement; a minister with no party affiliation does not count toward any market.

If no candidate is invested as Prime Minister within the period set by Article 99 of the Spanish Constitution and the Cortes are dissolved for a further election before any government is formed, the first official, stable formation of a government following that further election governs resolution.

Additional clarification(s):
Dissolution, absorption, or merger: If a party named in a market dissolves, is absorbed into, or merges with one or more other parties to form a new and distinct political party or organization prior to the relevant government formation, the originally named party shall not be considered part of government merely because its former politicians, officeholders, or assets have moved to, or been absorbed by, the new party. The resulting party is not treated as equivalent to the originally named party for purposes of this Contract, unless the circumstances instead satisfy the legal name change standard below, in which case that standard governs.
Legal name change: If a party named in a market undergoes a legal name change or rebranding but remains the same underlying legal political organization (i.e., the same legal registration, organizational continuity, and party structure persist, notwithstanding the new name), the renamed party continues to count as the same party named in that market.

markets.rules_secondary:
How this is resolved
Video of the the next Press Briefing by the White House Press Secretary (does not include gaggles), using the live broadcast or stream.
If a consensus by Kalshi employees cannot be reached using video, internal & external (official) transcripts of the the next Press Briefing by the White House Press Secretary (does not include gaggles) will be used.

Payout criteria 
Exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word. 
Plural nouns occurring within proper nouns and noun phrases (e.g. names, titles, etc).
Must be opened to the press for a live televised or streamed event to qualify.
White House Press Secretary speaking in an official capacity. 

Doesn't count for payout
Grammatical/tense inflections are otherwise not included. 
If White House Press Secretary is or is not present during a livestream, and does not speak in an official capacity the market will not qualify (e.g., inaudible private conversations on camera, unofficial statements picked up on a hot mic).
Except as otherwise specified, previously aired content, archival footage, and recordings captured at times, places, or events wholly separate from the featured address.

markets.rules_primary: If the House adopts the resolution adopting the Rules of the House of Representatives for the 120th Congress and that resolution prohibits Members from trading individual stocks after Issuance and before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A rule that prohibits Members from buying or holding individual stocks counts, even if it still allows Members to sell existing holdings with notice, place stocks in a blind trust, or invest in diversified funds such as ETFs or mutual funds. A rule need not cover spouses, dependents, the President or the Vice President.

The following do NOT count:
A separate bill or resolution, including one that the rules resolution only makes in order for a vote
A rule that only requires disclosure or advance notice of Members' stock trades
An announcement or plan to include a ban before the House adopts the resolution

If the House adopts the resolution adopting the Rules of the House of Representatives for the 120th Congress without such a prohibition, the market resolves to No; a later change to the House rules does not count.

Only reporting from the United States House of Representatives or any other Source Agency qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

markets.rules_primary: If the number of U.S. House seats won by Republican Party candidates is at least 158 in the 2026 U.S. House elections, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
A seat counts only if the relevant election authority records a Republican designation for the winning candidate’s candidacy in the November 3, 2026 general election; a recognized state affiliate, any one of several ballot lines, or a declared write-in candidacy so recorded all qualify. Caucus affiliation, endorsements and later party changes do not affect the count: a member elected without a Republican designation who caucuses with Republicans is not counted, and one elected as a Republican candidate who later leaves remains counted.

Only the regular general election in each of the 435 congressional districts for the term beginning January 3, 2027 counts; a special election for a 119th Congress vacancy is disregarded whenever held. No district counts twice.

Seats are counted from Designated Media Source calls as they stand at the Expiration time, not from House composition on any later date; the eight rank equally. A seat is counted when at least four have declared its winner with no contradictory declaration then outstanding; withdrawn or superseded declarations are disregarded. A seat not counted under that four-of-eight test is attributed to the candidate the state certifies as elected. A runoff seat is counted when that contest is called.

Designated Media Source declarations. For United States based elections, this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if (A) at least four (4) of the eight (8) Designated Media Sources have declared a winning candidate, party, or option, and (B) none of the Designated Media Sources have issued a contradictory declaration. “Designated Media Sources” are: The New York Times (NYT), The Associated Press (AP), Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), CNN, Fox News, NBC News, CBS News, and ABC News. Should one of the Designated Media Sources cease to provide independent election calls, it may be replaced at the sole discretion of the Exchange. For the purposes of this clause, a source declares a winning candidate, party, or option when it makes either (i) a formal projection of victory by its centralized decision desk, or (ii) an unambiguous statement in a news article that the candidate/party/option has won. For the network sources (Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC), a declaration from a local affiliate may represent the parent network; however, a declaration from the national desk shall always supersede any affiliate’s call. In all instances, a parent network and all of its affiliates shall collectively constitute a single source for the purpose of this clause.

Starting November 26, 2026, Kalshi will check each party's seat count every day at 10:00 AM ET using Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). Any market the results have decided will settle that morning; the rest will settle on February 1, 2027 as they do now. If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the event occurs.
markets.rules_primary: If the number of non-incumbent candidates endorsed by Elon Musk after Issuance who are elected to federal office in elections held before Nov 4, 2026 is at least 1, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market counts the non-incumbent candidates who receive explicit public endorsements from Elon Musk after Issuance (Jul 14, 2026) and before Nov 4, 2026 and who are subsequently elected to federal office in the United States in elections occurring after Issuance (Jul 14, 2026) and before Nov 4, 2026. Special elections count if they occur before Nov 4, 2026.

"Endorsed by Elon Musk" means an explicit statement of support posted by Elon Musk that unambiguously states he endorses, supports, or backs the specific candidate for the specific federal office. Retweets, likes, replies, or ambiguous statements do NOT constitute endorsements.

Making any monetary contribution (including in-kind contributions) to a candidate's campaign, political action committee, or affiliated organization, as reported by any Source Agency, is also considered an endorsement.

Participating in any of the following campaign activities for a candidate is considered an endorsement:
Speaking at a campaign rally, fundraiser, or official campaign event
Appearing in campaign advertisements or promotional materials
Serving in an official campaign role (e.g., campaign chair, advisor, surrogate)
Hosting or co-hosting a fundraising event

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if the specific individual leaves the role as defined in the payout criteria.
markets.rules_primary: If Mike Morath leaves (or announces he will leave) as Texas Education Commissioner before Feb 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This market resolves based on when the departure is publicly announced or officially communicated, regardless of the effective date.

An announcement counts if Mike Morath states he will leave the role, or if Gina Hinojosa or the Governor of Texas names the person who will replace him. Gina Hinojosa's pledges to fire him, including on Nov 3, 2026, and Mike Morath's Nov 5, 2026 statement about a transition to the next commissioner do NOT count.

Temporary leaves of absence, suspensions, or recusals do not constitute leaving, resigning from, or retiring from the role unless the individual formally and permanently ceases to hold the position. If the person vacates the role and then re-occupies the role, the contract may settle on the initial vacation of the role.

For "leave," cessation of holding the role qualifies, including resignation, retirement, removal, expulsion, expiration of term without renewal, recall, or other means by which the individual no longer occupies the role—this includes both voluntary and involuntary early departure AND the natural expiration of a term.

If the term expires but the person continues to serve in the role, the person has not left the role until the person stops serving, and a statement that his term ends or will not be renewed does NOT count unless it says when he will stop serving.

custom_strike.Combo: Democrats hold at least 240 seats in the House in 2027 + Democrats hold at least 54 seats in the Senate in 2027

markets.early_close_condition: This market will close and expire early if any component becomes impossible to occur (resolving to No) or all components have been satisfied (resolving to Yes).
markets.rules_primary: If ALL of the following occur: Democrats hold 240 or more seats in the House after the 2026 midterms AND Democrats hold 54 or more seats in the Senate after the 2026 midterms, then the market resolves to Yes.
markets.rules_secondary:
This is a combination market requiring ALL specified outcomes to occur for the contract to pay out. If ANY single component resolves to No or becomes impossible, the entire contract immediately resolves to No. Each component is resolved according to its corresponding Kalshi ruleset: "Will Democrats hold 240 or more seats in the House?" uses SEATSCONGRESS, "Will Democrats hold 54 or more seats in the Senate?" uses SEATSCONGRESS. All conditions must be satisfied on February 1, 2027.

This market will resolve based on the composition of the U.S. House of Representatives and the Senate on February 1, 2027. Individuals caucusing with either party will be included with them (e.g. an Independent who caucuses with a party, like Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders who caucuses with the Democrats, would be counted as a Democrat).

Clarification (11/12/26): Kalshi has filed an amendment that lets each seat-count leg of this combination event settle before February 1, 2027 once the election results have decided it. The combination settles Yes once every leg has settled Yes, or No as soon as any leg settles No. Starting November 26, 2026, each leg will be checked every day at 10:00 AM ET against Associated Press race calls, with a buffer for changes after the election (5 seats off the floor in the House, 1 in the Senate, and 1 seat added to the ceiling). If the composition of Congress on February 1, 2027 would have paid an early-settled market the other way, Kalshi will credit $1.00 per contract for positions held on that side at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026. Contracts bought after that time are not covered.

For example, as of November 11, 2026, the Associated Press has declared Democrats the winner of 254 House seats, with 13 seats undeclared. That gives Democrats a floor of 254 (seats declared) and a ceiling of 267 (254 plus the 13 undeclared), or 249 and 268 after the buffers. In KXDHOUSESEATS-27, every range from "Below 210" through "242-245" lies entirely below both values, so those markets would expire and settle No; "246-249" and "Above 249" each contain one of the two values, so they continue to trade and are checked again the next morning.
markets.title: Will Democrats hold 240 or more seats in the House after the 2026 midterms AND hold 54 or more seats in the Senate after the 2026 midterms?

important_info.markdown: **Important information:** Kalshi has filed an [amendment](https://kalshi-public-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/regulatory/notices/SEATSCONGRESS%2040.6%20Amendment%20Final.pdf) that allows each leg of this combination to settle before February 1, 2027, starting November 26, 2026, once Associated Press race calls have decided the outcome with a buffer for post-election changes. For positions held at 7:00 AM ET on November 12, 2026, if those positions would have been resolved in a trader's favor under the February 1, 2027 composition of Congress but early settlement changes that result, Kalshi will credit $1 per Contract held out of its own funds. A clarification for this market has been posted below.
